heading: The maternal lines
lead: Five women married into this line and carried it forward, and for years the front page said the same thing under each of them: «no archive of her own line yet». David asked on 29 September 2026 for that to stop being true. These are the pages; the research behind them is mostly still to do, and each page says exactly how much.

salomon.name: Salomon
salomon.gen: Generation two — she married Giovanni Battista Defranceschi (1787–1846).

rows.text: She was born on **17 March 1797** at **Gračišće**, and she married **[Giovanni Battista Defranceschi](/direct-line/)**, born 1787, died 1846. *(doc.)* **That is the whole of it.** *No parish entry for her marriage, no parents, no siblings, no death.*

rows.lab: ⚠ And one thing that is not nothing
rows.text:
This archive's pedigree carries a note about her family rather than about her: *«Of a family with a **palace on the square facing the bishop's**; by **1848** a **Salomon sat in the parliament at Vienna**.»* **So the Salomon of Gračišće were not peasants** — *they were a house with a building on the main square and, within a generation of Francisca, a seat in the Reichstag.* ⚠ **That note had no source attached to it in this archive.** *Half of it now has one.*

**The palace is real and it is dated.** *The **Salamon palace at Gračišće** stands on the square, is of the **sixteenth century — the date 1570 is given** — and its distinguishing feature is a row of **Gothic bifore, Venetian two-light windows, on the first floor**. It is in poor condition and wants restoration. (doc for the building; **the source describing it gives no family history and cites nothing**, so it establishes the palace and not the people.)*

**⚠ The parliament half is now settled, and it is WRONG.** *David downloaded the official roll of the **422 deputies of the first Austrian Reichstag, 1848–49**, and it was read here the same hour.* **There is no Salomon in it** — *437 lines, **65 surnames beginning with S**, **zero** matches for Salomon or Salamon in any spelling, with the control passing.* **(doc for the negative.)**

**And the seat the family remembered was real. It was their own.**

> **Defranceschi · Karl · k.k. Rathsprotokollist · Pisino · Küstenland**

*[**Carlo De Franceschi**](/carlo/) of Gologorica — the historian — **sat for the district of Pisino, Pazin**. **[The correction is recorded.](/corrections/)** *A family remembered a parliamentary seat correctly for a century and a half and attached it to the wife's people instead of its own.*

**Her parents are not here, and the registers that would name them are the Gračišće books being read film by film.** *A baptism of 17 March 1797 at Gračišće would give her father, her mother and the house number in one line.* ⚠ **But Gračišće is [absent from FamilySearch](/corrections/)**, as this archive established in September and forgot in September — *so this is a letter to **DAPA** or the **Poreč diocesan archive**, not a film.* **The same letter that would settle [Anton of Gologorica](/worklist/) could carry this.**

**⚠ And the book that would probably answer all of it in one go.** *[**Miroslav Bertoša, «Gologorički De Franceschi: između etosa i etnosa»**](/sources/), 1985 — **seventy-six pages** on this family by one of Croatia's leading historians of Istria. This archive's own source list calls it «**the most important single thing still unread**». **It is not online**; it is a 1985 book chapter and wants a Croatian library or interlibrary loan.* **A seventy-six-page study of the household Francisca married into is the likeliest single place for her marriage, her family and the palace to be discussed together.**

fernasar.name: Fernasar
fernasar.gen: Generation three — she married Antonio Defranceschi (1825–1894), the stonecutter of house 19.

paras: Born **17 October 1832** at **Gračišće**. She married **[Antonio Defranceschi](/direct-line/)** the stonecutter on 25 November 1856, and their son **Josip**, born 22 March 1863, is the man who took this line down off the Istrian karst to the Kvarner coast. *(**doc**.)*
Everything else about her turns on four letters, because **two hands wrote her surname and they do not agree**.

sections.lab: The pedigree's own wall note, against a register entry of 1862
sections.h2: Two hands wrote her surname, and they do not agree
paras: This archive's pedigree has carried the flag for a year: *«The surname is written **Fernasar** and **Tornasar** in different hands.»* **An F and a T in a nineteenth-century Istrian hand are not always distinguishable**, and the difference decides which family she belongs to and which entries in the register are hers.

And the second reading is not a copying slip travelling through this archive's own files. **A register entry of 1862 was read «Maria Tornasar»** and is recorded that way. Some scribe, somewhere, formed a letter that a careful reader took for a T. That reading is kept as a reading; what follows is about whether the *name* can be right.

sections.lab: Settled 29 September 2026 · the Austrian press, then two national surname databases
sections.h2: «Tornasar» is retired: it is printed nowhere, and borne by nobody
paras: **The press test came first.** Three spellings were run against the digitised Austrian newspapers. **«Tornasar» returns nothing at all** — not one issue. **«Fernasar» returns three**, and two of them are Austro-Hungarian casualty lists, which print a man's name, rank, regiment, **home commune** and year of birth:
> *Fernasar Josef, Inft., k. k. LIR. Nr. 5, 10. Komp., **Istrien, Pisino, Gračišće**, 1884; kriegsgef., Merw, Gebiet Transkaspien, Rußland.* — «Verlustliste», 6 May 1916

**Josef Fernasar, born 1884, of Gračišće** — taken prisoner and held at Merv in Transcaspia. The list gives province, district and commune, and the commune is **Maria's own village**, named in a printed record fifty-two years after she married out of it. *(A second issue, the wounded list of 14 December 1914, has a Josef Fernasar of the Pisino district born 1883 in hospital at Kassa with a kicked heel. **Whether that is the same man is not settled**: name, district and rough age agree; unit and year do not. Two cousins would look exactly the same.)*

**Today the question was put to two national surname databases**, because [the work list](/worklist/) predicted an atlas would decide the letter from the armchair. The full list of terms tried, with a control on each, is [in the search log](/searched/). In short: the **Croatian 2011 census** returns fewer than ten bearers — or none, it will not say which — for **Fernasar, Tornasar, Fernazar and Fornasar** alike, while returning **757 Poropat**; and **Cognomix**, which holds about 180,000 Italian surnames, has **no Fernasar and no Tornasar at all**.

**So the prediction was wrong, and it is worth saying so.** No atlas of the present can choose between two names that have both stopped existing. What the databases do is remove Tornasar's last possible support: it is borne by nobody in either country and printed in no issue of anything. **The reading stands as Fernasar** — on the press, not on the palaeography, which is still unread. *(**inf**, and firmly held.)*

**The person id is not changed.** `maria-fernasar-tornasar-de-franceschi` was minted when the question was open, and [ids are frozen here](/method/): a moved id is a dead URL. The id records what this archive believed when it minted it, which is the point of freezing them.

sections.lab: fornasâr — the man who works the kiln
sections.h2: And the commoner form of the name points at Friuli
paras: Beside the three Fernasar issues, the Austrian press holds **49 issues of «Fornasar»**, overwhelmingly in the same Pola paper. Fornasar is very probably the same name: Friulian ***fornasâr***, the man who works the kiln — a trade name, like *lapicida* on the other side of this marriage.

**And Fornasar is alive where that etymology says it should be.** Cognomix gives it about **25 families in Italy**: **Piemonte 11, Friuli-Venezia Giulia 8, Veneto 4, Liguria 1, Puglia 1**. Twelve of the twenty-five are in Friuli and the Veneto, which is the corner of Europe the word comes from. In Croatia it is under ten, like the rest — **the name did not stay in Istria**.

*The eleven in Piemonte are not explained here. Industrial migration to the north-west is the obvious reading and is **inf**, not doc.* And the step from Fernasar to Fornasar is itself still **inf**: two spellings in the same newspapers of the same province is a strong hint and not a document.

sections.lab: Four doors, and what is behind each
sections.h2: What is not known, and is worth asking for

asks.q: What letter did the priest actually form?
asks.a: **Her own baptism, 17 October 1832, at Gračišće — read as an image, not from an index.** Everything above is about whether the name can be right; none of it is about the ink. [The method this archive uses on a doubtful letter](/method/) is that a hand is only legible against itself: find the same scribe writing both candidate letters elsewhere in the same book, and compare at one magnification.

asks.q: Where are the Fernasar households at Gračišće?
asks.a: **The Gračišće status animarum**, which this archive has already read frame by frame for its own family. The Fernasar households will be on the same pages, and **nobody has looked for them**. Josef of 1884 is two generations below Maria.

asks.q: What is in the third Fernasar issue?
asks.a: ***Il Giornaletto di Pola*, 8 December 1914** — the one issue of the three that has never been read.

asks.q: A marriage in November, an eldest son in August
asks.a: The marriage is recorded **25 November 1856** and the eldest son Antonius is born **6 August 1856**, three and a half months earlier. Both dates are documented twice. This is a separate puzzle and it is not solved by settling the surname.

kovacina.name: Kovačina
kovacina.gen: Generation five — she married Anton Rudolf Defranceski (1890–1943), born at Klenovica house 22.

rows.lab: What is documented, and it is all German paper
rows.text: She is on the **Pfullingen list of foreigners in 1947**, and **certified by that town's mayor in 1950**. *(doc.)* **Every document this archive holds for her was made in Germany after the war** — *not one was made where she was born.*

The pedigree's wall note is blunt: *«Her parents are not in this archive. **Her own birth record has not been found** — «about 1890» is all the certificates give.»* **She is the only one of the five maternal lines whose birth year is an estimate**, *and the estimate comes from German certificates written fifty years after the event.* ⚠ **Her birthplace is not established either.** *(open.)*

**The [1948 window](/1948/) is already an open Arolsen question**, and her papers sit inside it — *the CM/1 file for the Pfullingen household is [reference 3.2.1.1, 32110000 058.158](/searched/), «Personal file of DEFRANCESKI, PETAR… **and of further persons**», and «further persons» is where a wife's own birthplace is usually written down.* **That file has not been read.** ⚠ *And she died at **Belgrade in 1975** — the same city where [her daughter Anka Nera](/worklist/) died in 1944, thirty-one years apart, and this archive still cannot say why either of them was there.*

source_maternal: The pedigree walls in this archive's own ancestors data, the Pfullingen and Arolsen material, and the Gračišće register programme. Written 29 September 2026 at David's request.
